h2: Pool Equipment Uluwatu – Pumps, Filters & Salt Systems
intro: Living on the Bukit means your pool equipment works under conditions most coastal properties never face: long suction runs, salt-laden air and hard limestone water. We install, repair and replace pumps, sand and cartridge filters, chlorinators, lights and auto-fill systems across Uluwatu so villa owners don't have to guess what's failing.

sections.h3: Why Pool Equipment Uluwatu Villas Wear Out Faster
sections.text: Uluwatu sits on dry limestone, so most villas pull water through long pipe runs from deep wells or large storage tanks. That extra strain wears pumps and pressure switches out quicker than you'd expect in flat coastal areas. Add constant salt spray rolling off the Bukit cliffs — especially around Bingin and Ungasan — and metal fittings, chlorinator cells and light housings corrode well before their normal lifespan. Hard limestone water then leaves scale inside filters and along tile lines, clogging flow paths.

sections.h3: Typical Jobs We Handle Around Pecatu
sections.text: The calls we get most often involve a pump that won't prime after a dry spell, a multiport valve sticking with salt deposits, or a sand filter simply due for fresh media. Chlorinator cells lose efficiency when surrounding air is this corrosive, and pool lights flicker or die as gaskets swell with trapped moisture. We cover installation, repair and replacement across all of these — pumps, cartridge and sand filters, auto-fill systems, lighting and chlorinators.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp for a Quote
sections.text: Before we can give you a fair figure, send clear photos showing the component in question: pump housing, filter tank label, valve position or light fixture. Include any model numbers visible on the unit, a short note on what changed (noise, pressure drop, discolouration), and whether the villa runs off mains, tank or well supply. If the issue comes and goes, a ten-second video helps enormously. Pricing depends entirely on the job; once we see the photos we'll come back with a straightforward number.

sections.h3: Prevention Tips Specific to the Bukit
sections.text: A few habits save real trouble up here. Rinse exposed pool equipment with fresh water after any strong onshore wind — two minutes of work, big payoff against corrosion. Check your float valve and auto-fill monthly so tanks don't overflow into the pump room. Every six months, inspect multiport valve O-rings and the chlorinator cell for scale; a quick vinegar soak keeps flow clean. If the strainer basket starts catching sand or debris more often, that's an early sign the filter media is breaking down.

faq.q: Does salt wind really damage pool equipment this badly?
faq.a: Yes — cliff-top villas get constant marine spray that corrodes metal fittings, chlorinator cells and light housings far faster than inland properties would experience.

faq.q: My pump keeps losing prime after rain. Is that normal in Uluwatu?
faq.a: With long suction runs from deep wells or large tanks on the Bukit, pumps work harder and internal seals degrade quicker; it's one of the most common issues we see across Bingin and Ungasan.

faq.q: How do I book a repair or installation?
faq.a: Send photos of the affected component plus any visible model numbers on WhatsApp along with a brief description of what changed, and we'll come back with a quote based on the specific job.
